title: Majestic Zugzwang
reviewNotes: Two branches, 18 exact positions from the complete seven-piece board. Nhf1, h4 and Kf7 build the queen cage; both illustrated queen-promotion choices lead to Nxf1, Nd2 and a winning h-pawn race. Qxf1 is the selected sacrifice, not the queen’s only legal move.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius would be able to win [music] from this incredible position. You see, black seems on the verge of winning this game because it has two pawns that are about to promote, and the white knight is also hanging. But, white has a majestic idea that is [music] going to allow him to win this game. The first move is knight H to F1, now attacking the pawn and forcing it to move. Now, black is only one step away from getting a new queen. But, white, instead of sacrificing the knight for that pawn, plays the very mysterious H4, a move that doesn't seem to make sense. Doesn't this simply allow the promotion to the queen? And the answer is, yes, it does. But, to understand this move, we have to look at what happens if black decides to take the knight and promote. This would actually be a mistake. After white recaptures, the black king has to remove the knight if it wants to promote. But, now knight is going to make sure that the pawn cannot promote, and the black king [music] is too late to stop the white pawn, so white would win. So, going back to that promotion, black has to realize that his best chance is to promote on G1, and now the knights are powerless. The black queen is going to be able to stop the white pawn and win the game, and black is going to be simply out of the woods, right? Well, not exactly because white has an incredible and completely [music] unexpected move in this position. The beautiful king F7, paradoxically stepping away [music] from the action, but a shiver goes down the spine of the player with the black pieces after he realizes that there isn't a single safe square for the black queen to go to. Everything is covered either by the knights or by the pawn and by the king, and the black pawn and the king are stuck, meaning that this is a zugzwang. The only way for black to win this would be to not make a move. But, of course, black has to play a move. But, after queen takes F1 and knight takes F1, we're going to end up in that same position. Knight D2 is going to make [music] sure that black cannot promote, and the black king is just too far from the white pawn. White is going to promote >> [music] >> and win this game.
